 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Amit Bansal
 Order

By way of the present petition, the petitioner seeks leave to appeal against the Judgment dated 3rd June, 2009, whereby the petitioner was acquitted of the offences under Sections 353/186 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 in FIR No.90/88 registered at Police Station Lahori Gate and the offences under Section 16(1)(c)(d) read with Section 7 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 in Complaint Case no.158/89.
2.

This Court vide order dated 26th July, 2023 had directed the learned APP to obtain instructions with regard to the number of days for which condonation of delay can be sought in filing a leave to appeal petition.
3. Learned APP submits that she could not obtain instructions from the department with regard to the same.
4. A perusal of the impugned order reveals that Food Inspector could not collect the sample of 'Kali Mirch Whole' from the shop of the accused as the mob gathered outside the shop of the accused.
Food Inspector in his cross-examination has admitted that when the sample was demanded from This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 16/09/2023 at 17:17:15 the accused, he did not object even upto the stage of sealing and packing the sample bottles and signing the documents.

There is no cogent and reliable evidence to show that the accused snatched Delhi Administration vs Rajinder Goel on 6 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4699073/
1 the sample bottles and documents and prevented the Food Inspector from collecting samples.
5. Further, the impugned judgment was passed on 3rd June, 2009.
However, the present leave petition was filed before this Court on 28th April, 2015.
No reasons have been given by the appellant in the application filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963 for condonation of delay of more than five years in filing the leave petition.
6. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances, no grounds for the grant of leave to appeal are made out.
7. Accordingly, the leave petition is dismissed.

AMIT BANSAL, J.
SEPTEMBER 6, 2023 rt
